I’ll first read the scoped project policies and then inspect the flyer generation path to find where dummy data is introduced. After that I’ll patch only the relevant source sections and avoid runtime/server commands as requested.

The local policy is broad, but the BuilderX envelope narrows this to the flyer PDF-data issue and brand colors. `rg` is unavailable in this container, so I’m using `find`/`grep` for focused discovery.

The relevant app is a generated React page. The current handoff explicitly says the PDF is only used for its filename and the profile content comes from `catalogData.js`, so I’m going to replace that dummy-data path with local PDF text extraction feeding the existing flyer layout.

There’s no PDF library in the project and package files are off-limits for this task. I’m implementing best-effort browser-side PDF text extraction from the uploaded file bytes, then deriving the flyer fields from that real extracted text with a clear error/status path if the PDF has no accessible text layer.

I’m going to patch `catalogData.js` with extraction helpers and defaults, then update the page to store the extracted flyer state instead of rendering the hardcoded profile arrays. I’ll add minimal CSS for status/extracted-text details and keep the existing Navy Glass palette.

The page now derives its rendered profile, metrics, skills, and timeline from extracted PDF text state. I’m adding a compact status/details presentation so users can see whether the flyer is actually using PDF content, without changing the existing layout sections.

I found the generated docs still claimed the app does not parse the PDF, which would now be wrong. I’m updating only those generated handoff notes/metadata so the project state matches the implemented behavior.

I’m tightening the PDF reader so it can also attempt text extraction from Flate-compressed PDF streams when the browser supports native decompression. That keeps the change dependency-free while covering more real exported PDFs than filename-only or raw-byte matching.
The extraction helpers are now in place, including a fallback for compressed streams where available. I’m doing static checks only, respecting the no npm/Vite/runtime validation constraint.

One remaining static string still used the word “dummy,” so I removed that as well. I’m also adding support for the other common PDF text-showing operators so the local reader has a broader chance of extracting real CV text.
The code check passed for the extracted-data helper module. I’m cleaning the remaining wording and source literals so the generated handoff no longer refers to dummy candidate content.
I’m running one last static pass for syntax and stale dummy-data references. I’m not starting the app or running npm/Vite per the BuilderX constraints.

The helper module passes `node --check`, and stale dummy-data wording is gone. One portable file-list command failed because this BusyBox `find` lacks `-printf`; that does not affect the app changes, and I’m using simpler checks instead.

Implemented the scoped flyer fix.

- [src/generated/generatedPage.jsx](/workspace/money/apps/protfolio-flyer/src/generated/generatedPage.jsx): wired upload state to extracted PDF content instead of hardcoded data, with status/error handling and extracted-text review.
